summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, bilateral lower extremity amputations, chronic kidney disease, and systolic heart failure was admitted for left ear pain and swelling concerning for malignant otitis externa. Imaging showed soft tissue induration without bone erosion, and she was treated for cellulitis with broad-spectrum antibiotics, later narrowed to linezolid and ciprofloxacin with oral vancomycin for C. diff prophylaxis. Her hospital course was complicated by sepsis, acute kidney injury with hyperkalemia, and anion gap metabolic acidosis, all of which improved with supportive care. Her home lisinopril was held, insulin regimen adjusted, and carvedilol and atorvastatin initiated for cardioprotection. She responded well, with infection resolution, renal recovery, and stable vital signs, and was discharged home with outpatient follow-up, lab monitoring, and a plan to complete antibiotics and restart medications as directed.
problems: Acute kidney failure with lesion of tubular necrosis
